summary: Plausible and cheap: a prepare()-time, synthetic-data, graph-replay pick among cuBLASLt's own heuristic candidates at exact m=128/256. The not-landed NN-layout probe already showed cuBLAS has a faster pooler m=128 algo (22.9 vs 25.0 us, 128x64 split-K). Attribution comes from the printed prepare() table, so no companion is needed. One precision guard must be added: split-K algos that reduce in bf16 have to be excluded.
justification: A. The mechanism is plausible. The FINDINGS profile has pooler verify_16 at 25.2 us on one nvjet_sm90_tst_64x64_64x13_2x1 (no split-K, ~2.7 TB/s vs the 14.6 us floor). unpooler verify_16 is 19.7-20.0 us vs 14.6 and qkv_gate verify_16 is 17.0 us (12.9 us nvjet 96x64 split-K plus a 3.1 us splitKreduce) vs 8.4. The strongest support is bf16-m128-nn-weight-layout-probe (done/neutral, not on master). Handing cuBLAS an NN problem made it pick nvjet 128x64_64x8_1x2 split-K for pooler m=128: 22.9 vs 25.0 us, +9.2%. unpooler m=128 went 19.1 vs 20.1 us (+5.1%). So better nvjet configs exist for these exact shapes, and heuristic-0 for TN is not the best one. Enumerating heuristic candidates for TN is a direct way to reach them without the 4x-weight transposed copy. The expected directions match TASK.md. verify_16 is one of six equally weighted loads (~76 us of non-router time), so ~3-5 us saved is ~+0.7-1.2% on the headline. That is inside the ~1.5-2.5% run drift, so the run must be judged by per-shape rows and the prepare() table, not the headline. The spec already says this. The verify_32 'flat' expectation is right: the NN probe moved pooler m=256 only +3.4% and qkv_gate m=256 lost 5.7%. The 3% keep-threshold protects those rows. Weakest link: whether cublasLtMatmulAlgoGetHeuristic for the TN descriptor returns anything beyond near-duplicates of result 0. On sm90, nvjet heuristics often return only a handful of entries. The qkv_gate 'faster' expectation is the weakest row: in the NN probe, cuBLAS still chose 96x64 split-K plus a separate splitKreduce (16.8 vs 16.8 us). Nothing shows a non-split-K or in-kernel-reduce candidate with a full-K tile that beats it at n=2304, k=8192, m=128. A secondary weak point: the incumbent row in prepare() goes through torch/cublas (cublasGemmEx-style heuristic). The candidates come from the Lt heuristic API, whose index 0 need not equal the incumbent. That is harmless, because the incumbent is timed directly. But 'candidate 0 == today's kernel' should not be assumed when reading the table.
confounders: sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity: defines the incumbent (_bf16_gemm_dispatch_impl at m=128/256), which is the exact comparison point inside prepare(). It does not confound; it is the control. If it were absent, the starter's x @ W[:n].T would issue the same TN cuBLAS problem anyway.

router-triton-hilo-fused-control-splitk-all-m / router-hilo-at-m8: different layer, timed as separate shapes; router rows are byte-identical. Any router verify_16/verify_32 movement is run drift, as in the combo's harvest (router verify_1/16 0.92/0.94 on identical code).

bf16-shape-gated-triton-winners-combo: touches only m<=16 (plus the unpooler n==1024 slice). Disjoint from the m in {128,256} keys this change adds, so it cannot interact on any scored shape. The prepare()-allocated Triton workspaces and warmups do not share the Lt workspaces.
interference: C. No companion is warranted. No landed hypothesis touches the m=128/256 bf16 path, so an ab-revert has nothing to revert. The change carries its own attribution: prepare() prints, per (layer, m), the incumbent time, the best candidate time and the choice, so every changed row in the scored output pairs with a logged non-incumbent pick. Where 'incumbent' was kept, that row is byte-identical to master. A control that isolates a sub-change would mean re-running one key alone, which the per-row table already resolves. A gain is readable as 'rows with a pick got faster'. A loss on a picked row is readable as 'the prepare() timing did not transfer to the judge's timing', and that is itself the finding. A flat run with all-incumbent picks settles that cuBLAS's heuristic list holds nothing better for TN. The closest open question is the overlap with the NN-layout probe's pooler/unpooler m=128 gains. That is a later combo decision (take whichever row is faster), not a companion for this run.
rules_flags: PRECISION, must fix in implementation: cuBLASLt heuristic candidates can include split-K algos whose CUBLASLT_ALGO_CONFIG_REDUCTION_SCHEME is CUBLASLT_REDUCTION_SCHEME_INPLACE or OUTPUT_TYPE. Those reduce split-K partials in the bf16 output type, which is lower precision than SGLang's fp32 accumulation (the incumbent uses splitKreduce_kernel<..., float, ...>). The rel-L2 1e-3 filter may not catch a 2-way split. Set CUBLASLT_MATMUL_PREF_REDUCTION_SCHEME_MASK to (CUBLASLT_REDUCTION_SCHEME_NONE | CUBLASLT_REDUCTION_SCHEME_COMPUTE_TYPE) in the heuristic preference. Also reject any returned algo whose CUBLASLT_ALGO_CONFIG_SPLITK_NUM > 1 with a reduction scheme other than COMPUTE_TYPE (read via cublasLtMatmulAlgoConfigGetAttribute), and print the split-K number and reduction scheme in the table.

Timing-based selection in prepare(): I do not judge this genuinely ambiguous. The rules make prepare() untimed for up to 300 s and forbid work outside the timed calls (computing or caching outputs), caching or replaying outputs, and tampering with timing. Choosing a GEMM algorithm by shape from synthetic randn inputs computes nothing that kernel_fn returns, and depends on nothing in the scored inputs. It is the same as Triton autotune or PyTorch TunableOp, and it is upstreamable. In-workspace precedent: muse_decode_layer pooler-gemm-splitk-autotune (job 2e1a43ab85324776) did the same prepare()-time graph-replay pick, was reviewed 'proceed', passed and was harvested neutral. torch.cuda.Event in prepare() measures; it does not patch the harness's timing. If the human wants a standing ruling, record one in PENDING_USER standing answers, but it should not block this run.

load_inline is explicitly sanctioned by the technical rules. Build note: with cpp_sources only, torch.utils.cpp_extension.load_inline defaults with_cuda to False and will not add the CUDA include and library dirs that ATen/cuda/CUDAContext.h and cublasLt.h need. Pass with_cuda=True (plus extra_ldflags=['-lcublasLt']). This is the first load_inline in any submission in this workspace, and bf16 has 1 check left today. Wrap the build in try/except so a build failure falls back to master's path with a printed reason rather than failing the run. The table will then show 'build failed' instead of silently matching master.

Graph capture and host syncs: cublasLtMatmul on the current stream with a prepare()-allocated workspace is capturable. Descriptors and layouts must be created before capture: create them in prepare() or on first use outside capture. Creating them inside a capture is a host-side op and is fine, but kernel_fn must not call cudaMalloc or sync. Use torch.empty for out (the caching allocator is graph-safe). Do not call .cpu() on algo_row in kernel_fn: keep the algo rows as a CPU tensor (or Python bytes) in state and pass the host pointer, not a CUDA tensor.

Branching: kernel_fn keys on (layer, cfg m) only, both fixed config fields, so this is allowed. Exact-m keys mean the test shapes (m=130 unpooler, m=33 o, etc.) and the final review's nearby shapes take master's path. That is safe for correctness and for the 'much slower on nearby shapes' check.
open_questions: How many candidates does the TN heuristic actually return per key at requestedAlgoCount=32? If <=3 near-duplicates, the follow-up is to enumerate cublasLtMatmulAlgoGetIds plus CUBLASLT_ALGO_CAP tile, split-K and stage options with cublasLtMatmulAlgoInit/ConfigSetAttribute and cublasLtMatmulAlgoCheck. That space contains the 128x64_64x8 split-K tile the NN probe found for pooler. Print the count per key so this is answerable from the log.
Does the incumbent's measured kernel (via torch) appear among the Lt candidates? Print each candidate's tile and split-K attributes so the table can be matched to the profile's nvjet names.

Is prepare()'s single-kernel median (event pair per replay after a 256 MiB flush) close to the judge's per-shape median? The judge's reported time includes ~2-4 us per graph node for nvjet+splitKreduce pairs (LESSONS). A candidate that adds a separate reduce node can look better in prepare() than in the judge if the events bracket only the kernel. Bracket the whole graph replay, as specified, and prefer the 3% margin to be measured that way.

Could torch.cuda.tunable (TunableOp) with an offline-recorded result file loaded in prepare() achieve the same without load_inline on this image? Probably not worth it on CUDA, but it would remove the compile risk.
